supporting_observations.claim: The recurring HTTPS proxy CONNECT requests in the supplied records are to updates.pixelforge-suite.com, an update service approved in the environment context.
The successful requests recur at roughly five-minute intervals, from 13:37:50 through 14:07:46 UTC; the 13:42:31 request was rejected with proxy status 407.
The network connections to the explicit proxy for these update checks are attributed to C:\Program Files\PixelForge\pfupdater.exe, matching the approved updater path.
The updater process was launched from the approved PixelForge installation directory under leo.martins's session.
Taken together, the observed cadence, destination, and process attribution are consistent with the approved PixelForge update checks and do not support a malicious finding for the alerted activity.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records show CONNECT destinations, status, byte counts, and durations, but do not expose the HTTPS application payload.
The provided records show recurring updater connections beginning at 13:37:50 UTC; they do not independently document every connection described by the alert for the entire 13:30–14:10 interval.
claims_not_established: The content or purpose of data exchanged inside the HTTPS tunnels is not visible in the supplied proxy records.
The supplied records do not establish whether the updater retrieved or installed an update.
unrelated_findings: DropboxUpdate.exe ran as SYSTEM on WS-LMARTINS-01, although Dropbox is not listed among approved software or services. Investigate separately; the supplied records do not tie it to the alerted PixelForge connections. (T046-00119, T046-00120, T046-00127, T046-00128)

A network authentication for sam.okafor originated from WS-LMARTINS-01, whereas the environment context says remote administration is only done from WS-SOKAFOR-01. Investigate separately; this does not establish a connection to the alerted HTTPS activity. (T046-00023, T046-00024)

FILE-NWD-01 initiated an RPC connection to WS-LMARTINS-01 on port 135. This is separate from the alerted outbound HTTPS activity and may merit review against the stated remote-administration practice. (T046-00063, T046-00067, T046-00068, T046-00069)
